To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the penalized quasi-contrast method is consistent for the detection of multiple change-points in a large class of causal time series.

we provide a consistent estimator of the number of changes, change points and parameters of the models, in the general case, when the time series is a causal time series with a large class of parameters.
we provide a new method for change-point detection in time series that is consistent and achieves the optimal convergence rates for a large class of semiparametric models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of detecting change points in a time series model, where the parameters change at each instant.
the detection of multiple change-points in a general framework of time series.
multiple change-point detection for time series.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is able to detect the change dates and to estimate the parameters in the models of AR($\tau$), GARCH($\tau$) and T-GARCH($\tau$, $\tau$).

, for a given sample size, our method provides a more precise estimator of the change dates, a better estimate of the number of changes and a more precise estimation of the parameters than any other existing method.
our method provides the best results for the change point detection in the case of general causal time series.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to detect multiple changes in a large class of time series, and that we have proved the consistency and the rate of convergence for our estimator.
we have extended the change point detection theory for independent random variables to the case of causal time series.
we propose a new approach for multiple change point detection in a semparametric model and we show that the method is very competitive with respect to other methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of penalized contrasts allows us to detect changes in the coefficients of the AR($\inpsilon$), ARCH($p$) and TACRH($p$) models.
, in the presence of multiple change-points in the parameters, the estimation of the model can be achieved by a simple penalized quasi-liklihood approach.
the penalized contrast is a powerful tool for the multiple change-point detection, especially for non-linear processes.
